Roman emperor from 306 to 337 and the first to become a Christian. He was born at Naissus, today's Niš in Serbia, son of Constantius, one of the rulers of the Tetrarchy. When his father died at York in 306, the army there proclaimed him emperor.

  • In 312 he beat his rival Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge and took the west.
  • In 313 he and Licinius agreed the Edict of Milan, giving Christians freedom of worship.
  • In 324 he defeated Licinius and ruled the whole empire.
  • In 325 he called the Council of Nicaea to settle a quarrel over the nature of Christ.
  • In 330 he dedicated a new capital on the Bosporus, Constantinople.

He also issued a gold coin, the solidus, that stayed stable for centuries. He gave churches money and land, though he was baptised only on his deathbed. His turn to Christianity and his new city shaped the next thousand years of Europe and the Near East.
